title: A hidden leak in solids - Nature Energy
gist: A News & Views commentary by Seoul National University's Noh and Kang flags that two new studies overturn the assumption solid electrolytes fully block electronic conduction, showing residual electronic conductivity drives self-discharge in solid-state batteries at open circuit — especially in thin, practical-format cells — and sets limits needed for long shelf life.

insights.claim: Solid electrolytes have long been assumed by the battery field to block electronic conduction entirely while allowing fast lithium-ion transport, an assumption that underlies most solid-state battery safety and stability claims.
insights.speaker: Joohyeon Noh and Kisuk Kang
insights.so_what: This is the baseline assumption solid-state battery developers (and investors evaluating them) have relied on; the piece signals it needs revisiting.
insights.quote: Solid electrolytes have long been treated as materials that block electronic conduction while enabling fast lithium-ion transport.

insights.claim: Two new studies show that residual electronic conductivity in solid electrolytes can drive self-discharge in solid-state batteries even at open circuit (i.e. when the battery is sitting idle, not connected to a load), which is a previously underappreciated failure mode.
insights.speaker: Joohyeon Noh and Kisuk Kang
insights.so_what: Self-discharge at rest is a direct threat to shelf life and calendar life claims solid-state battery makers use to court EV and consumer-electronics customers — a due-diligence question to raise with any solid-state battery vendor.
insights.quote: Two studies now show that residual electronic conductivity can drive self-discharge in solid-state batteries at open circuit, particularly in thin practical cells, and identify the limits needed to ensure long shelf life.

insights.claim: The self-discharge effect from residual electronic conductivity is particularly pronounced in thin, practical-format cells, as opposed to thicker lab-scale test cells, meaning the problem could be worse in commercially relevant cell geometries than in typical academic demonstrations.
insights.speaker: Joohyeon Noh and Kisuk Kang
insights.so_what: A red flag for anyone extrapolating solid-state battery performance from thick lab coin cells to thin commercial-format cells — the effect may not scale the way vendors imply.
insights.quote: Two studies now show that residual electronic conductivity can drive self-discharge in solid-state batteries at open circuit, particularly in thin practical cells

insights.claim: The two underlying studies identify quantitative limits on electronic conductivity that solid electrolyte materials must meet to ensure long shelf life in solid-state batteries, implying an emerging materials-selection criterion for the field.
insights.speaker: Joohyeon Noh and Kisuk Kang
insights.so_what: Watch for solid electrolyte material screens to start reporting electronic-conductivity ceilings alongside ionic conductivity — a new benchmark investors can use to compare vendor claims.
insights.quote: identify the limits needed to ensure long shelf life
